Outbound access

How is network reachability scoped?

The exact schema gives workspace-write a network_access flag that defaults false, and the 0.90.0 release announces a policy-enforcing network sandbox proxy. Current security docs describe sandbox, approval and network controls as separate layers; that rolling statement is not back-projected to runtime behavior in 0.90.0.

Record limitations

  • All substantive behavior statements are publisher-attributed; the catalog did not download, install or run Codex CLI.
  • Exact-version claims use the 0.90.0 release or tagged repository source; rolling security documentation is not treated as exact-version evidence.
  • Publisher-provided artifact digests were recorded from official metadata but were not independently recomputed.
  • Configuration alternatives identify possible authority surfaces, not the effective settings or enforcement of any session.
  • The Overeager Coding Agents paper is not included as independent evidence because evaluator independence, disclosure and public-artifact gates did not all pass.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The package, binary, platform build, architecture, installation path and executable digest used by any real session.
  2. The effective approval policy and whether every consequential shell, file, app, connector, MCP and collaboration action is covered.
  3. The effective sandbox mode, writable roots, operating-system enforcement, escape resistance and behavior outside the working directory.
  4. The effective network flag, network-proxy state, policy rules, DNS path, WebSocket handling, destinations and subprocess coverage.
  5. The configured connectors and MCP servers, their tools, annotations, credentials, data access, side effects and destinations.
  6. The active Coding or Plan mode, plan-to-execution transition and mode-specific tool authority.
  7. The use, lifetime, persistence and complete provenance of ephemeral or spawned collaboration threads.
  8. The selected model, provider, endpoint revision, reasoning settings, authentication path, request payload and data handling.
  9. The contents, permissions, retention, encryption, backup and deletion behavior of local configuration, credentials, history and logs.
  10. Which current rolling security statements also applied to 0.90.0 beyond what the tagged schema establishes.
  11. Whether the Overeager Coding Agents evaluators are genuinely independent after complete funding and conflict disclosure.
  12. Whether the promised benchmark, audit bundle, adapters, annotations and exact environment artifacts become publicly inspectable and reproducible.
